question: Could lower-notional optionable instruments mechanically fit the current capital policy?

answer.explanation: Under the measured Paper policy a cash-secured put needs collateral = strike x 100 below the ticker hard-veto threshold (strike <= 224.99 for ALLOW_REDUCED, <= 149.99 for full-cap sizing). That is arithmetic and is true of any optionable underlying whose listed strikes sit below those levels. No offline dataset in this repository enumerates optionable instruments with prices other than the archived SPY chain, so which named instruments actually have listable, liquid, in-policy puts cannot be established offline. The existing audit documents only that IYM, KORU and ZSL had share prices below roughly 225 without recording the prices. Capital fit is also only one gate: every instrument other than SPY is blocked today by the owner-approved manifest (not approved) and by the missing relative-strength policy, independent of capital.

capitalPolicyBasis.collateralFormula: strike x multiplier(100), single multiplier, dollars
capitalPolicyBasis.note: Figures are recorded from the cited document, not re-measured here (no provider call).
